_about: The narration of the Noncredit Summit film's narrated cut, draft 1 (S335 SkyMotion, 2026-10-05). Sam, 2026-10-05: "do one version with just music and another with voice over from our ElevenLabs narrator. See if we have access to a female voice with a slight hispanic accent." One to three plain sentences a scene, written from the deck's slide scripts (CPLBrain 20261005_Noncredit_Summit_CPL_Slides_1.md), every figure the film's: 52,394 served (said as more than fifty-two thousand), 7,500 a year by 2030, one in four, 29,649 (said as nearly thirty thousand), the 34% worded as the deck's .md gives it, 8 and 8.5 and 22 units, 21 colleges, 78% at 28 colleges, 49 at 253 sites, $35 million and $2 million, $50,000 grants, $1.8 million. Funding vocabulary: funding, max award; never earn for an institution, money or pool. The voice says the figures in words and writes MAP as map, so the captions and the aligner read what she says; the captions write MAP back. Draft 2 (S339 SkyReel, 2026-10-06): the voice is Sarah Explains, the narrator goes unnamed, the title opens on Sam's greeting, the funding opens on a short celebratory line, the ongoing funding is $7 million, and the learners follow deck draft 2 (Nadia's three CompTIA certifications at 9 units as at Saddleback College; Mt. San Antonio College plans to document its ladder).

engine.name: elevenlabs
engine._why: Sarah Explains is an ElevenLabs library voice: "approachable, conversational, and informative. Great for explainer videos, narration, e-learning". Sam picked her by ear on 2026-10-06 (S339 SkyReel: "Let's go with 3 voice") from four auditions of the title and funding lines (Vivie 2, Cassandra, Sarah Explains, and the premade Sarah), after asking for "another female voice in standard English. A little upbeat in tone--not over the top." She replaces ladypatty1 (S335). The same day he asked that the narrator go unnamed: "Let's take out naming the narrator Sierra and make her anonymous." A library voice's owner can withdraw it, so the clips are committed here and a re-read needs the voice still listed (creative_list_voices). One generation per scene through the ElevenLabs connector. narrate.py brings every clip to -20 dBFS speech RMS.

layout._why: The funding film's narrated pacing: each scene is its lead-in (the seam, its barrier and the first reveal), its clip, and its air.

scenes.text: Greetings, Noncredit CPL Heroes! It's a great day for our system as we continue to build out our shared CPL tools to serve noncredit learners. Special thanks to our legislative partners, who supported the Board of Governors' and Chancellor Christian's request for an additional thirty-five million dollars in CPL funding. Here's how noncredit learning becomes college credit.

cues.why: the title, Noncredit learning, college credit, letter by letter, as the greeting names the room

scenes.air_why: The title's picture runs 5.7 s past its first letter (the letters, the subtitle, the seam); the air lets the subtitle and the seam land after the greeting's last line. Sam, 2026-10-06, wrote the greeting: "Start with Greetings Noncredit CPL Heroes. It's a great day for our system as we continue to build out our shared CPL tools to serve noncredit learners. Special thanks to our legislative partners who supported the Board of Governor's and Chancellor Christians request for an additional $35 million CPL funding..."

scenes.text: Last year, Chancellor Christian said that noncredit and not-for-credit learners would be key to our CPL goal. Our colleges have served more than fifty-two thousand students through CPL so far. By twenty thirty, CPL for about seventy-five hundred noncredit learners a year is within reach.

cues.why: her 2025 words, word by word
the goal track and its label, students served through CPL
the count landing on 52,452
the line Within reach by 2030: CPL for about 7,500 noncredit learners a year

scenes.text: About one in four of our students takes a noncredit course each year. More than thirty thousand students earned a noncredit award in twenty twenty-four to twenty-five. And noncredit students who were working before they enrolled saw their median quarterly wages rise thirty-four percent a year after finishing or leaving their program.

cues.why: the first figure, 1 in 4
the count landing on 30,795

cues.word: And noncredit students who were working
cues.why: the third figure, +34%, and its line

scenes.text: Mira's free noncredit community health worker courses at Cabrillo College mirror credit courses. She earned eight units of credit and a Certificate of Achievement without retaking a class.

cues.why: the first step, the mirrored courses
the gold step, 8 units of CPL
the third step, the certificate

scenes.air_why: The path's last step, the note under the portrait and the footnote follow the certificate by 3 s of picture, and the voice ends 1.6 s after naming it; without the air the gold step and the certificate lead their words by 1.0 s.

scenes.text: Emilio earned his EMT certification through Moreno Valley College's noncredit program. The college awards eight and a half units for it, toward a paramedic or fire technology degree and on to a bachelor's in emergency management.

cues.why: the first step, EMT training and certification
the gold step, 8.5 units of CPL

cues.word: a paramedic or fire technology degree
cues.why: the third step, the associate degree
the fourth step, the bachelor's degree

scenes.air_why: The note under the portrait and the footnote follow the last step by 1.6 s of picture, and the voice ends as it names the step; without the air the last step leads its words by 1.0 s.

scenes.text: Carla climbed Mount San Antonio College's noncredit health ladder to the LVN license. College of the Desert awards twenty-two units for that license toward an associate degree in nursing, and Mount San Antonio College plans to document its own ladder.

cues.why: the first step, CNA then medical assistant or surgical technician
the second step, vocational nursing and the LVN license
the dashed step, 22 units of CPL for the LVN license, which Mt. San Antonio College plans to document
the fourth step, the ADN

scenes.text: Nadia is finishing a noncredit IT support certificate at North Orange Continuing Education. She holds three CompTIA certifications, A plus, Network plus and Security plus. Twelve colleges award credit for all three, and at Saddleback College they carry nine units toward an associate degree in information technology.

cues.why: the first step, the noncredit certificate
the second step, CompTIA A+, Network+ and Security+
the CPL step, 9 units for all three, as at Saddleback College
the fourth step, the credit certificate and associate degree

scenes.air_why: The note under the portrait (twelve colleges award credit for all three) and the footnote follow the last step, and the voice ends as it names the step; the air lets them land.

scenes.text: Faculty have already said yes. At twenty-eight colleges, seventy-eight percent of eligible EMT units reach a transcript, and forty-nine statewide credit determinations sit ready at two hundred fifty-three college sites. Most of the opportunity is still ahead.

cues.why: the heading
the count landing on 78%
the count landing on 49
the closing line

scenes.text: Now, something to celebrate! The state budget provides thirty-five million dollars one-time and seven million ongoing for CPL. Last year, fifty-thousand-dollar grants went to four noncredit programs. This year, one point eight million dollars in noncredit funding reaches every community college noncredit program. Credit and noncredit FTES together size every max award.

cues.why: the count landing on $35 million
the line one-time, and $7 million ongoing
the card Last year, $50,000 grants
the card This year, $1.8 million
the closing line, noncredit counts from the start

scenes.open_why: Sam, 2026-10-06: "Add a short celebratory phrase before announcing the funding." Four grants: his revised funding slide names North Orange Continuing Education, Mt. San Antonio College, San Diego College of Continuing Education and Calbright ("2,3,4 y", 2026-10-06).

scenes.text: Three invitations to the field. Mirror a course. Post your certificates in map. Invite your completers back. The CPL Initiative team will help you with each one. Our time is now!

the first invitation
the second invitation
the third invitation
the line The CPL Initiative team will help with each one
